findings.title: Descent as a time-bounded process
findings.claim: The focus's descent of water is an initiating movement whose visible yield has a function-bound duration: it produces growth and then releases it into scattering, while the wider lasting-garden imagery supplies a live contrast rather than a replacement.
findings.mechanism: The carrier is أَنزَلْنَٰهُ at 18:45:7:1. The focus's separate growth and dispersal occurrences, together with the independent 18:1, 18:107, and 18:108 comparisons supplied by the retained evidence, make the n-z-l carrier contact a wider distinction between process input, temporary yield, and lasting lodging.
findings.reader_payoff: The water's descent becomes the beginning of a timed material process, so the scene reads as more than a static rain image while the ordinary parable remains recoverable.
findings.containment: The finding concerns the function and duration of this descent in the supplied scene; it does not say that every descent ends in dispersal, equate the water with revelation or the afterlife, or turn the attributed 18:1 comparison into a new lexical branch.

epistemic.reason: The carrier branch is accepted and the focus anchor is exact. The cross-run support is trusted, while the reader-walk comparison and its 18:1 reference remain legacy-unbound; the resulting relation is retained with that qualification visible.
